scope_protection.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person to practice or attempt to offer to practice optometry, as defined in this act, without having at the time of so doing a valid, unexpired, unrevoked and unsuspended license issued under this act.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure of an applicant to demonstrate the necessary qualifications as provided in this act or board rules.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure of an applicant for licensure to demonstrate the necessary qualifications as provided in this act or the rules and regulations of the board.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to permanently display the license or a certified copy in any location where the optometrist practices.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to permanently display in any location in which he practices a license or a certified copy of a license issued by the board.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Use of deceit or fraud in obtaining a license or in the practice of optometry.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Use of deceit or fraud in obtaining a license or in the practice of optometry.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Making misleading, deceptive, untrue or fraudulent representations or advertisements in the practice of optometry.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Making misleading, deceptive, untrue or fraudulent representations or advertisements in the practice of optometry.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction of a felony or a crime involving moral turpitude.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conviction of a felony or a crime involving moral turpitude. Conviction shall include a finding or verdict of guilt, an admission of guilt or a plea of nolo contendere.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Revocation, suspension, refusal to grant a license, or other disciplinary action by a proper licensing authority of another state, territory or country.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Revocation, suspension or refusal to grant a license to practice optometry, or imposition of other disciplinary action, by the proper licensing authority of another state, territory or country.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Being unable to practice with reasonable skill and safety to patients by reason of illness, drug/alcohol addiction, felony conviction under Controlled Substance Act, or mental incompetency.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Being unable to practice the profession with reasonable skill and safety to patients by reason of illness, addiction to drugs or alcohol, having been convicted of a felonious act prohibited under the act of April 14, 1972 (P.L.233, No.64), known as "The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act," or convicted of a felony relating to a controlled substance in a court of law of the United States or any other state, territory, possession or country, or if he or she is or shall become mentally incompetent.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violation of a regulation promulgated or order issued by the board in a previous disciplinary proceeding.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violation of a regulation promulgated or order issued by the board in a previous disciplinary proceeding against that licensee or applicant for licensure.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Knowingly aiding, assisting, procuring or advising an unlicensed person to practice optometry.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Knowingly aiding, assisting, procuring or advising an unlicensed person, or person who is in violation of this act, or the rules and regulations of the board, to practice optometry.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to conform to the acceptable and prevailing standards of optometric practice in rendering professional service to a patient.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to conform to, the acceptable and prevailing standards of optometric practice in rendering professional service to a patient. Actual injury to a patient need not be established.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Neglect of duty in the practice of optometry, including failure to refer a patient to a physician when appropriate.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Neglect of duty in the practice of optometry, which may include failure to refer a patient, when appropriate, to a physician for consultation or further treatment when an optometric examination determines the presence of a pathology.

insurance_required.quote: To require every licensee to insure liability by purchasing and maintaining professional liability insurance coverage in accordance with the following provisions: ... a licensee shall obtain and maintain, to the satisfaction of the board, professional liability insurance coverage in the minimum amount of $200,000 per occurrence and $600,000 per annual aggregate.

methods_authorized.quote: The use of any and all means or methods for the examination, diagnosis and treatment of all conditions of the human visual system. The term shall include: (i) The examination for, and adapting and fitting of, any and all kinds and types of lenses, including contact lenses. (ii) The administration and prescription of all legend and nonlegend drugs, either by topical or oral routes of administration, approved by the board in section 4.3 for the treatment of the eye, the eyelids, the lacrimal system and the conjunctiva ... (iii) The removal of superficial foreign bodies from the ocular surface or adnexa. (iv) Epinephrine auto-injectors for anaphylaxis. (v) The ordering and interpretation of angiography via noninvasive imaging, which shall only include optical coherence tomography. (vi) The administration and prescription of all legend and nonlegend drugs approved by the board under section 4.3 for the treatment of glaucoma.

drug_authority.value: Optometrists may prescribe and administer all legend and nonlegend drugs by topical or oral routes of administration approved by the board for treatment of the eye, eyelids, lacrimal system and conjunctiva, including codeine and hydrocodone combinations (Schedule II limited to 72-hour supply), and drugs for the treatment of glaucoma. Schedule I and Schedule II controlled substances are excluded except for codeine and hydrocodone combinations. Therapeutically certified optometrists may prescribe and administer pharmaceutical agents for therapeutic purposes after board certification.
drug_authority.quote: The administration and prescription of all legend and nonlegend drugs, either by topical or oral routes of administration, approved by the board in section 4.3 for the treatment of the eye, the eyelids, the lacrimal system and the conjunctiva, including codeine and hydrocodone combinations ... The prescription of Schedule II controlled substances containing codeine and hydrocodone combinations may not exceed a 72-hour supply.
